# Intercept exploration (synthetic)

Original synthetic teaching extension of lesson_lineplot_rise.md. No learner evidence.

## LESSON

### Predict a vertical shift

Objective SYN-LINE-EXPLORE: explain why equal changes to an intercept move every plotted point by the same amount.
Source SYN-LINE-EXPLORE: original synthetic example in this file.

> [!EXAMPLE]
> [LINEPLOT: 1,0,2]
> Prediction: Start with y = x + 0. Predict which points at x = -2, 0, 2 move when the intercept changes to 2, and predict whether the slope changes.
> Manipulation: Commit your prediction, then try intercepts 2, 1, 0 and -1. Compare the row for x = 0 with the other two rows. Keep x fixed when comparing rules.
> Static explanation: The original points (-2, -2), (0, 0), (2, 2) become (-2, 0), (0, 2), (2, 4) for y = x + 2. Adding 2 raises every y by 2. The difference between neighboring y values stays 2, so the slope stays 1. Explain why the intercept changes the whole line even though its name mentions the y axis.
> Transfer: Put the controls aside. A different rule is y = -x + 1. Predict its y values at x = -2, 0, 2, then predict all three after the intercept decreases to -1. Explain which quantity determines direction and which determines the starting y value.

### Explain the comparison

> [!EXAMPLE]
> [COMPARE: 12,18,24,mm]
> Hold the invented observation interval fixed. A records 12 mm and B records 18 mm, so B minus A is 6 mm. Predict when the quantities will be equal, then adjust B. Explain why changing B changes the difference while A stays fixed.

Without the controls, compare A = 9 mm with B = 7 mm. State the signed difference and explain what its sign means. This original example is synthesis for practice, not an assessment.

Q1. In an invented color inventory, which label names the violet tile? (difficulty: recall)
[OBJECTIVE: synthetic:inventory.label]

A) amber tile
B) teal tile
C) violet tile
D) white tile

CORRECT: C

WHY BEST: The inventory identifies the violet tile by its own label.
KEY DISCRIMINATOR: Match the named color to the label.
DISTRACTOR ANALYSIS:
- A) This would be correct if the requested tile were amber.
- B) This would be correct if the requested tile were teal.
- C) Correct: this is the named inventory label.
- D) This would be correct if the requested tile were white.
TRAP: Choosing a different color from the invented inventory.
CONFIDENCE: high
